subject: FintechCo: Multi-region performance comparisons & next tests
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo — quick recap & proposed next tests (geo perf)

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick notes and agreed next steps from the call: 

- Goal: validate multi-region performance and data residency constraints for your payments reconciliation workloads (p99 latency under 250ms in primary regions; ability to keep EU traffic in EU).
- Current hypothesis: Redwood can meet latency targets with our dedicated routing + regional model copies; hyperscaler endpoints you tested hit higher egress and cold-start variability.
- Data residency: you need logs/audits retained in-region for 365 days for EU payments. We offer VPC-private deployment and can keep audit logs in customer-managed storage.

Agreed next tests (we'll run these over the next 7–10 days):
1) End-to-end latency sweep from your EU and US offices against the same model version (we’ll provide a small harness).
2) Bypass caching and then enable prefix/KV caching to show tail improvements.
3) Comparative run vs one hyperscaler endpoint (you said AWS Bedrock was the most relevant) using the same prompt set and identical token limits.
4) Verify that audit logs from EU traffic can be retained in your EU S3-like bucket (we'll provide a sample retention config).

I'll loop Marissa in to coordinate the test harness and share the initial scripts + expected metrics. Please confirm Priya (security) should be included on the audit/logging thread.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192
\

From: Alex Torres <alex@fintechco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — quick recap & proposed next tests (geo perf)

Thanks Jordan — this looks good. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- We want the latency sweep to include our EU production region (Frankfurt) and two US regions (us-west-2 and us-east-1). Can you also include a Singapore vantage to understand APAC tail behavior (even though APAC is lower priority)?
- For the hyperscaler comparison, yes let's use the Bedrock endpoint we tested earlier. Important that requests are identical (same prompt, temperature, max tokens).
- Priya is on the thread for logging and SOC-related items. She'll want to see what audit fields you capture and whether they include requester IP, model version, and redaction metadata.

Also — timeline is important. We want initial numbers before our internal infra review on the 12th.

Alex
Alex Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, FintechCo
alex@fintechco.com | +1 (212) 555-0134

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex@fintechco.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechco.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — quick recap & proposed next tests (geo perf)

Alex — looping in Sean (solutions eng) to own the harness and collection. We kicked off a short perf harness that will: 

- Run 1k requests per vantage (Frankfurt, us-west-2, us-east-1, Singapore) using the exact prompt set you shared on the call. 
- Capture client-to-edge RTT, edge-to-service RPC, and token-generation p50/p95/p99. 
- Run against: (A) Redwood hosted regional replicas, (B) Redwood routing to dedicated US-only pool, (C) AWS Bedrock (your test endpoint).

I attached our initial CSV and trace bundle for transparency — the CSV has per-request timing and the traces include sample KV-cache hit/miss markers. We’ll anonymize requester IPs before sharing anything back to you.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-latency-20260707.csv; multi-region-traces-20260707.zip

Next steps: Sean, can you run the first sweep tomorrow and share p50/p95/p99 + a short summary? Jordan — I’ll prepare the audit-retention config sample (SOC2-extract-request.pdf) for Priya.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0178
\

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 14:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — quick recap & proposed next tests (geo perf)

Alex / team — first sweep complete. High level findings below (attached CSV + traces): 

Summary (all tests used the exact prompt payload and token limits you provided):
- Frankfurt (eu-central-1) against Redwood regional replica: p50 68ms, p95 180ms, p99 240ms.
- us-west-2 (Redwood routed to dedicated pool): p50 45ms, p95 120ms, p99 165ms.
- us-east-1 (Redwood regional replica): p50 52ms, p95 130ms, p99 190ms.
- Singapore (APAC): p50 95ms, p95 270ms, p99 410ms (APAC shows higher tail; we can improve with a closer replica).

Bedrock (your test endpoint) — single region (us-east-1) run provided by you: p50 70ms, p95 210ms, p99 380ms. Notes: Bedrock exhibited higher p99 tail in our test and more variance between runs (cold-start visible at the start of the sweep).

Cache impact test (Redwood): enabling prefix/KV cache reduced eu-central-1 p99 from 240ms to 130ms in our sample runs for repeated prefixes.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-latency-20260707.csv; multi-region-traces-20260707.zip

Action items:
- Marissa: provide the EU audit retention snippet for Priya.
- Jordan: propose a canary plan for a small EU footprint run (50k tokens/day) to collect production-like metrics.
- Alex/Priya: confirm whether you want us to share anonymized traces with your SRE for deeper analysis.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
\

From: Alex Torres <alex@fintechco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — quick recap & proposed next tests (geo perf)

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the data — this is very helpful. A few responses: 

- The p99 numbers for EU look promising, and the cache impact is compelling. Please go ahead with the small EU canary (Jordan — we sign off on 50k tokens/day for 2 weeks).
- Priya: please see the SOC2-extract-request.pdf Marissa mentioned. Priya — let us know any missing fields on audit retention; we need that to clear our compliance gate.
- We’d like anonymized traces shared with our SRE team. I’ll open a ticket and share the contact — give me a line and I’ll attach the HubSpot ticket id.

Next steps: Jordan — can you send a short canary plan (rollout, metrics, rollback criteria) and an expected date to start? We’re aiming to start the week of 13 Jul to align with our infra review.

Thanks,
Alex
